title: Reseat a dropped bicycle chain
instruction: Feed the dropped chain onto the front teeth. Withdraw the guiding hand and turn the crank for at least two revolutions with the rear sprocket driven throughout.
context: A dropped bicycle chain can be restored by guiding its upper run back into the tooth plane while turning the crank.
setup: Single-speed bench drivetrain with a 54-pitch chain (12.70 mm pitch), independently rotating 28/16-tooth sprockets 201.76 mm apart, a 42.46 mm radius catcher, and 1 mN·m rear drag. Reset the front chain 11 mm inboard. Two YAM arms use a pedal socket and a lift pick.
scoring: Native pocket occupancy, all 54 roller identities, uninterrupted 28:16 drive for two crank turns, and pedal socket withdrawal. See README.md for thresholds and negative controls.
reset_notes: Thread the rear sprocket. Rest the front half-wrap on the inboard catcher. Remove the spacing gauge and let the chain settle. See README for dimensions and checks.
fidelity: Simulated roller-to-tooth contact and constrained link pitch. Roller axes are parallel and side plates simplified. Proposed physical build has not been tested.
scores: Scripted deep-drop repair 1.00; fresh command replay 1.00; idle 0.00; crank-only 0.00. Revised Dream-1 result pending.
